title: Philippines extends 14-day visa-free privilege for Chinese nationals
summary: The Philippines has extended the 14-day visa-free entry privilege for Chinese nationals for another year, from Jan. 16, 2027 until Jan. 15, 2028, the Department of Foreign Affairs announced yesterday.

blocks.text: The DFA said the extension is in line with President Marcos’ directive to boost international tourist arrivals and investments in the Philippines, while maintaining existing immigration and national security safeguards.

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines has extended the 14-day visa-free entry privilege for Chinese nationals for another year, from Jan. 16, 2027 until Jan. 15, 2028, the Department of Foreign Affairs announced yesterday.

“Under the arrangement, Chinese nationals may be granted visa-free entry for a stay not exceeding 14 days, exclusively for tourism or business purposes. The privilege remains non-extendible and non-convertible to any other Philippine visa category,” the DFA said.
Eligible travelers must possess a passport valid for at least six months beyond their intended stay, confirmed hotel accommodation or booking and a return or onward ticket.

The DFA explained that the extension remains subject to existing immigration and security safeguards, including the allowed entry of Chinese nationals availing themselves of the visa-free entry privilege through the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) in Metro Manila and Mactan-Cebu International Airport (MCIA) in Cebu only.
Travelers must comply with applicable eTravel registration requirements and have no derogatory records with the Bureau of Immigration (BI).

The admission into the Philippines, according to the DFA, remains subject to inspection, screening procedures and determination by the BI, including applicable identity verification, watchlist checks and risk-based assessment.
“The DFA will continue to coordinate with the BI and the law enforcement agencies on the monitoring of the implementation of the 14-day visa-free arrangement for Chinese nationals,” the DFA said.
The DFA also advised that Chinese nationals transiting through the Philippines and intending to enter the country en route to a third destination must obtain the appropriate Philippine transit visa.
The Department of Tourism welcomed the decision to extend the visa-free entry privilege of Chinese nationals until 2028.

According to DOT, Chinese arrivals to the country have increased by 70.18 percent and have reflected renewed visitor interest. Despite the brewing dispute in the West Philippine Sea, China remains one of the country’s largest source markets in 2026, ranking fourth at 6.87 percent. — Andrew Ronquillo
